fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of Tetralogy of Fallot, but can also be seen in other right heart obstructive lesions.

fact_rationales.F12: The single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of ventricular septal defects, but can also be seen in other septal defects.
fact_rationales.F15: The enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of a left-to-right shunt, which is most consistent with a ventricular septal defect.

fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur can be seen in various cardiac anomalies, but the presence of a systolic ejection murmur is more characteristic of truncus arteriosus due to the single blood vessel coming out of the heart.
fact_rationales.F15: An enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is indicative of increased blood flow to the lungs, which can be seen in total anomalous pulmonary venous connection and truncus arteriosus due to the abnormal connections of the pulmonary veins or a single blood vessel coming out of the heart, respectively.

fact_rationales.F11: Nasal flaring, costosternal retractions, and perioral cyanosis are signs of respiratory distress, which can be seen in various cardiac anomalies, particularly those with increased pulmonary blood flow.
fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus but can be seen in other cardiac anomalies.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is consistent with total anomalous pulmonary venous connection and truncus arteriosus.
fact_rationales.F9: Tachycardia is a nonspecific finding but more commonly associated with transposition of the great arteries.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome due to the underdeveloped left heart structures.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome due to the increased flow and pressure in the pulmonary circuit.

fact_rationales.F12: Cardiac auscultation findings are more indicative of a cardiac issue rather than a non-cardiac cause.
fact_rationales.F15: Chest imaging findings suggest a cardiac pathology, making non-cardiac causes less likely.
